chunks: What Sahl ibn Ziyad narrated from Isma'il ibn Mihran, who said:

I wrote to al-Rida عليه السلام: Our companions have mentioned that when the sun passes the meridian, the time of zuhr and 'asr has entered; and when it sets, the time of maghrib and the later 'isha has entered, except that this one is before that one in travel and residence; and that the time of maghrib is until a quarter of the night.

So he wrote: The time is as such, except that the time of maghrib is narrow, and the end of its time is the disappearance of the redness and its turning into whiteness on the western horizon. As for the time of the later 'isha, it is the falling of the redness from the west according to what we have mentioned, and its end is one-third of the night or half of the night; and that is in cases of necessity and when there are excuses.
Many of the reports that we presented earlier have included this, because most of them include mention of the time of the two prayers, and that further clarifies it.

key_terms.أُفُقِ الْمَغْرِبِ: the western horizon where twilight signs are observed
key_terms.الْأَعْذَارِ: valid excuses or extenuating circumstances affecting prayer timing
key_terms.الْمَغْرِبِ: the maghrib prayer at sunset and its time period
key_terms.ثُلُثُ اللَّيْلِ: one-third of the night as an upper limit mentioned for 'isha
key_terms.ذَهَابُ الْحُمْرَةِ: the disappearance of the twilight redness marking the end of maghrib
key_terms.نِصْفُ اللَّيْلِ: half of the night as an upper limit in cases of excuse
key_terms.وَقْتُ: the legally designated time for an act of worship

ai.seo_question: When does the time of maghrib end and the time of 'isha begin according to Imam al-Rida عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses the legal timings of maghrib and 'isha prayers, affirming that the prayer times begin as described by the companions while clarifying that the time of maghrib is narrow. It specifies that maghrib ends with the disappearance of the redness in the western horizon, and that the later limit for 'isha extends to one-third or half of the night in cases of necessity or excuse.
